newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy set to miss Maastricht targets - employers.
newsitem.headline: Italy set to miss Maastricht targets - employers.

text.p: Italy is set to fall well short of the economic criteria established in the Maastricht Treaty for countries wishing to join the single European currency, Italian industrialists' group Confindustria said on Tuesday.

In a report on the economy, Confindustria predicted that without further budget action, the ratio of budget deficit to gross domestic product would be 4.8 percent in 1997 against Maastricht's three percent target.
The ratio this year will rise to 7.5 percent from 7.39 percent in 1995, Confindustria said.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi's government has unveiled a budget for next year that aims to cut the deficit by a massive 61.5 trillion lire, which it says will bring the deficit/GDP ratio down to the magic three percent level.
Confindustria said this hope would be dashed, partly because the government would have to cover a big overshoot in its 1996 accounts.

"On the deficit/GDP ratio, the uncertainty is not over if Italy will reach the three percent target but over how much it will overshoot," Confindustria's chief economist Giampaolo Galli told reporters.
Confindustria said the state deficit this year would be 140 trillion lire against government expectations of 123 trillion lire at the time it prepared the 1997 budget. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
